title: Slow Magnetic Relaxation in an Asymmetrically Coupled Heptanuclear Dysprosium(III)–Nickel(II) Architecture

material_class.structural_family: asymmetric heptanuclear Ni4Dy3 core of three edge-sharing Dy2Ni triangles plus one Dy2Ni2 rectangle

synthesis.procedure: Triethylamine (0.056 mL, 0.4 mmol) was added to H2L (0.2 mmol, 42.6 mg) in methanol/acetonitrile (10 mL/5 mL). The mixture was sonicated for 1 h. Solid Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.1 mmol, 45.6 mg) and Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.1 mmol, 29 mg) were added and the yellow solution was stirred for 1 h. Slow evaporation without disturbance afforded rod-shaped dark greenish-brown single crystals after one week.
synthesis.time: sonication 1 h, then stirring 1 h; crystals after 1 week
synthesis.vessel_or_method: sonication followed by stirring and unperturbed slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The reaction mixture was left unperturbed to allow slow evaporation; rod-shaped dark greenish-brown single crystals formed after one week.

properties.summary: DC susceptibility of 1 shows χMT = 50.61 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (vs 45.51 cm3 K mol−1 expected for three Dy3+ and three Ni2+), remaining fairly constant to 20 K then rising to 55.04 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, suggesting intramolecular ferromagnetic interactions within the Dy3Ni3 magnetic core (one NiII treated as diamagnetic). Magnetization vs H/T curves are not superimposed, indicating anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states; M reaches 23.21 μB at 1.9 K and 70 kOe without saturation. Zero-field AC data (3 Oe, 3–1200 Hz) show frequency-dependent χ″ below 25 K (onset of slow relaxation) but no χ″ maxima above 2 K up to 1200 Hz, attributed to fast quantum tunneling. The compound is described as an Ln–Ni SMM with a unique asymmetric Ni4Dy3 architecture.

measurements.name: out-of-phase AC susceptibility (χ″)
measurements.value: frequency-dependent signal below 25 K; no maxima above 2 K
measurements.conditions: zero dc field; 3 Oe AC field; 3–1200 Hz
